_: The UI's own text, English. Keys are what the apps ask for; a key missing here falls back to the built-in English. Copy this file to add a language: assets/i18n/<code>.json, then set ui_language to <code>.
tabinfo.status: The state of this installation at a glance: the database, the job queue, the providers and their credentials, and a hash lookup. Nothing here changes data; each card links to where things are done.
tabinfo.collection: Everything the catalogue knows and what you hold of it, from the game as a whole down to the bytes on disk.
tabinfo.collection.titles: a game as a whole on one platform, with every release of it under it (regions, revisions), and what was made from it: hacks and translations, patches, trainers, saves; shown with the name and art of its first release.
tabinfo.collection.releases: one per platform and name as the DATs list them (USA, Japan, Rev 1 …), with the dumps each DAT source has of it. Every version of one hack or translation is one release.
tabinfo.collection.games: what you hold, grouped from your files: one per release and disc set, complete when a DAT's dump of it is fully present.
tabinfo.collection.roms: one dump of one disc or cartridge you hold, which may be several files (a cue and its bins).
tabinfo.collection.files: the files in your directories, as the last scan found them.
tabinfo.collection.contents: bytes identified by hash wherever they are: a file on disk, or a member inside an archive (a CHD's tracks, a zip's files).
tabinfo.collection.sets: your own ordered lists of releases, like playlists: for copying a group to another machine, or just grouping.
tabinfo.collection.crossplatform: one row per IGDB game, whichever platforms it is on here.
tabinfo.collection.definitive: one row per game with its ports, remakes and remasters, led by its definitive version.
tabinfo.collection.multimedia: audio, video and photo discs the DATs list: music CDs, DVD-Video, Blu-ray, Video CD, Photo CD.
tabinfo.collection.documents: manuals, magazines, books, game guides and scans the DATs list.
tabinfo.collection.etc: what is made around a console that is not a game: map packs, tools (dashboards, emulators, editors, installers), trainers and saves.
tabinfo.collection.patches: patch files: RetroAchievements' compatibility patches with their download, patch files the DATs list, and your own in a patch directory.
tabinfo.collection.bios: a machine's own system files: BIOS, firmware, DSP ROMs, NAND and SD-card dumps, from DATs and from your scans, with their platform. None of them is a title.
tabinfo.collection.audio: soundtracks and other music tagged to titles, with the player.
tabinfo.ra: Your RetroAchievements account and the games that have achievements, as of the last account sync.
tabinfo.ra.titles: the games with achievements (all of them, or only those held here: ra_source_default), with your progress.
tabinfo.ra.mastery: games you mastered: every achievement, in hardcore.
tabinfo.ra.complete: games you completed: every achievement, in softcore.
tabinfo.ra.in_progress: games you have started (at least one achievement earned) but not mastered or completed. Beaten games are included too, unless ra_include_beaten is off.
tabinfo.ra.to_play: your Want to Play list on RetroAchievements.
tabinfo.edit: Your own corrections to the catalogue, kept apart from imported data so a re-import or a provider sync does not undo them.
tabinfo.edit.keywords: your keyword tags. A tag is put on a title and covers all of its releases, so the Titles, Releases and Games lists can all be filtered by it. Rename, join or remove tags here.
tabinfo.edit.merges: every merge of one title into another, automatic or yours; split a title back out here.
tabinfo.edit.orders: titles whose releases you put in your own order; reset them to the default order here.
tabinfo.edit.merge_review: suggested merges and regroupings IGDB's grouping misses (International and Director's Cut releases, translated names, bundles of single games), one at a time.
tabinfo.edit.aspect_review: the 4:3 / 8:7 (or square-pixel) question of each game still open, one title at a time.
tabinfo.jobs: Start syncs, checks and other long work, and follow what the worker runs. Jobs run on the server's worker and carry on with no browser open; a failed job keeps its error in the list. Scans have their own tab.
tabinfo.data: Where the catalogue comes from, and the database underneath it.
tabinfo.data.providers: metadata and media services (IGDB, ScreenScraper, RetroAchievements …): credentials, how much of each is held, and syncs.
tabinfo.data.dats: the reference DAT sources the catalogue is built from: sync (download + import), import the downloaded files offline, and download or upload the files. hacks, homebrew and etc are filled by upload or by copying DATs into their folders.
tabinfo.data.db: the database tables row by row, maintenance (DB optimize) and CSV exports.
tabinfo.schedules: Jobs that run on their own: a scan, a DAT or provider sync, a backup and so on, every so often or when a provider reports a change.
tabinfo.config: How this installation is set up: its folders, emulators, copying, storage, settings, server, backups, sharing with other machines, mode and user accounts.
tabinfo.server: A client's way into its main server's own screens (its jobs, accounts and settings), after signing in with an account on that server.
tabinfo.about: This version and its release notes.
tabinfo.config.directories: the folders this machine scans: ROMs, patches, audio and so on, each with its type and platform.
tabinfo.config.emulators: the emulators a rom can be opened with, per platform (not tested yet).
tabinfo.config.copy: how copies name their folders and which archive format they convert to, per platform.
tabinfo.config.storage: where media, audio and temporary files go, and how much space is kept free.
tabinfo.config.settings: every setting as a form, by section.
tabinfo.config.settings_json: the same settings as raw JSON, plus keys the form does not know.
tabinfo.config.server: the server's ports, start and stop, and the database cache.
tabinfo.config.backup: database and catalogue backups (make, download, upload, restore), the phone cache, and the configuration as a file to export and import.
tabinfo.config.share: the main server and peers this machine syncs from.
tabinfo.config.mode: standalone (builds its own catalogue) or client (takes it from a main server).
tabinfo.config.users: the accounts that may sign in, and what each may do.
tabinfo.config.credentials: API keys and accounts for the metadata and art providers; the same form as on Data › Providers.
explain.status.database: Where this installation lives: the app root (the install folder), the MariaDB server and database it uses, how many directories are set up and how many files they hold.
explain.status.jobs: How many jobs are in each state: pending (waiting), in progress, done, failed, cancelled. Jobs lists them.
explain.status.providers: The metadata and media providers. A faded icon has no usable credentials or is off; hover it for why. Credentials are set under Data › Providers.
explain.status.lookup: Finds the release a hash belongs to: paste a CRC32, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 or RetroAchievements hash. Leave the algorithm on auto, or pick it.
explain.status.tables: How many rows each database table holds. Click a table to browse it (Data › DB).
explain.list.ownership: The bar on a row's left edge (the top edge of a card): green, held here (and on the main server, in client mode); yellow, held here or on a peer but not on the main server; grey, on the main server only. No bar: nobody holds it.
explain.collection.titles:
One row per game on one platform, with all its releases. View: the whole catalogue with what you hold first, the whole catalogue, or only what you hold. Kinds: tick what counts as a release here (commercial, translations, hacks, mods, homebrew, arcade ports, WiiWare, RetroAchievements subsets); a title is listed when any ticked kind matches, and "guessed language" finds the patched releases whose language is a guess.

Hacks and translations are under the game they were made from, in a Patched ROMs section on its page. "patch links" lists the ones put there by name alone, to confirm or unlink one, several or all.

Right-click a title, or select several, for what can be done with them (keyword tags, merging and more).
explain.collection.definitive:
One row per game: the base game together with its official ports, remakes, remasters and editions (Complete, GOTY) and the collections that hold it. Patches, fan translations, DLC and standalone expansions are not part of it. The tab lists the versions within your catalogue. A version no DAT lists (a PC, PS5 or Switch 2 version) appears, like a game you don't hold, only when its platform's IGDB metadata is synced. Syncing the modern platforms (PS4/5, PC, Switch 1/2, Xbox One/Series, iOS, Android) takes much more storage and makes each job much longer. Instead, definitive_fetch_versions (Config › Settings) can fetch the other versions, older and newer, of each game you hold on disk; versions on platforms you don't collect then appear too.

The definitive version is the newest one; between versions out on several platforms, your platform priority decides (Config › Settings), and a PC version takes the "PC (Definitive tab)" place unless it is much older than the newest. Open a row to drag its versions into the order you want.

Show: lead each row with the definitive version or with the base game; the other one is in the next columns. The two-cover grid shows both covers on one card.
explain.definitive.notes: Version note: a filter for games where the latest version might contain less content than an earlier one. S: the older version is strongly recommended. A: which is better depends on preference. B: an older version has content the latest lacks, but the latest is still the better one. The note is on the game's page.
explain.collection.releases:
One row per release as the DATs list it: region, languages, version, the DAT sources that have it and the providers it is linked to. Kinds: tick the kinds to list; any ticked one matches.

A badge says what a release is when it is not a commercial one (translation, hack, mod, homebrew …). "suggested" means it was put under its game by name alone. A "?" after a language means the language is a guess. Every version of one hack or translation is one release, and holding any version is holding it.

Right-click a release for more, such as adding it to a set or copying it.
explain.collection.games: What you hold, grouped from your files: one row per release and disc set. Complete means a DAT's dump of it is fully present; incomplete ones say what is missing on their page.
explain.collection.roms: One row per dump you hold of one disc or cartridge, which may be several files (a cue and its bins).
explain.collection.files: The files in your directories as the last scan found them, with the hashes it took and what they matched. A file that is gone is kept as a record, so a moved or restored copy is recognised.
explain.collection.etc:
What is made around a console that is not a game: map packs, tools (dashboards, emulators, editors, installers), trainers and saves, from the DATs of the etc source. Kind narrows the list to one of them.

Trainers, saves and map packs are also listed on the page of the game they are for, when it is in the catalogue.
explain.collection.patches:
Every patch file the catalogue knows of. RetroAchievements: its compatibility patches, with the same download as on its game pages. DAT: patch files a DAT lists. My files: files in a directory of type "patch" that are neither.

"patches" names the game a patch is for, when that is known.
explain.collection.bios:
BIOS, firmware, co-processor (DSP) ROMs and other system files, with the platform each belongs to. They are not games, so they have no title and are not in Titles or Releases.

DAT rows are entries a DAT lists as a BIOS or firmware (retrobios, No-Intro's [BIOS] entries, the BIOS DATs of Redump and TOSEC); held means a scanned file matches one. An emulator's support files retrobios carries (an archive, a sound) are listed as other system files.

My files is everything you hold: the DAT entries your files match, and the files a scan identified as a system file that no DAT lists (a NAND or SD-card dump, a BIOS no DAT has).

A directory of type bios reads every file this way; a rom directory picks out the system files among the games.
explain.ra.account: Your RetroAchievements account and your progress, as of the last account sync. Without an account (ra_username and ra_api_key in api.env) this tab stays empty.
explain.ra.list: Games: every game with achievements, or only those held here. The base filter groups by console or by genre. Views: a list, covers, or RetroAchievements' own icons, title screens, screenshots and badges.
explain.jobs.other: DAT sync downloads the reference DATs and imports what changed. DB optimize purges soft-deleted rows; it is rarely worth it, and its prompt says why. Media relayout moves media downloaded by an older version into the current folder layout.
explain.jobs.list:
Every job, newest first, with its progress. Jobs run on the server's worker in lanes: one at a time per lane (one per provider, CPU work, DAT downloads, backups), the lanes side by side. Click a job for its full result; a failed one keeps its error.

"+ queue" beside a job's button adds it to wait its turn instead: it starts when nothing else is running or waiting, so a list of queued jobs runs one after another (a DAT sync, then the Hasheous dump, then IGDB). Such a job shows "in turn" while it waits. "clear from the list" removes finished jobs (done, failed, cancelled), by status or the selected rows; a pending or running job is never removed.
explain.data.imports: The latest DAT imports: when, which source and platform, which file, the DAT's own name and version, and how many games and files it declared.
explain.data.dat_sources:
Where the reference DATs come from. Most sources are downloaded by a DAT sync; Lost Level Archive is one of them.

hacks, homebrew and etc are not downloaded: they hold the DATs you upload here or copy into their folders, and "import downloaded" on their own row reads them. A sync or import of all sources leaves them out. romexplorer_dbtool make-dats turns a folder of community DATs into files for them.

After an import the title merge pass runs: it folds the versions of one patched work into one release and links each to the game it was made from.
explain.data.maintenance: DB optimize purges soft-deleted rows (rarely worth it; the prompt says why). The counterparts CSVs list each release's USA / English counterpart per platform. DAT sync downloads and imports every source except hacks, homebrew and etc.
explain.data.tables: Every table with its row count and columns. Click one to browse its rows, sort them and filter by a column.
tabinfo.scan: Scan directories and match them against the DATs, and watch the files being read right now.
explain.scan.form:
Full: soft-deletes the directory's file rows first and re-adds what the walk finds. Quick: only files without a row yet. Rehash: no walk, re-reads the files already recorded.

Hash match (new): only games with no link yet, and files the services have not been asked about. Hash match (all): every game again. The links it is about to re-make are removed first (DAT links, and hash / name / fuzzy provider links), and cached "not found" answers are asked again. Manual and exact links stay.

DAT: links each game to the DAT release its files match. Hasheous: looks the files up by hash (an archive by the track or ROM inside) and links the IGDB, RetroAchievements, ScreenScraper, SteamGridDB, MobyGames and TheGamesDB ids it reports. PlayMatch: the same by hash for files whose IGDB id is still unknown, then searches by name for titles any provider is still missing (IGDB, TheGamesDB, SteamGridDB, MobyGames, EmuReady, ScreenScraper), and fetches metadata for every id found.

A platform is recorded only when the file's own signature confirms it; anything else stays unknown until a hash match identifies it.
explain.scan.running: Each running scan, with the files it is reading right now: how many run at once is set by scan_parallel_files under Config › Settings. A running title merge pass is shown too, with each of its steps: done (with what it did and how long it took), running, or still to come.
explain.jobs.media_backfill: Downloads the media types switched on in media_download that a linked game does not have yet: for the games you own, or for the whole catalogue. Only providers a game is already linked to are asked. It first puts back art that is on record but missing on disk (after a database restore, or when a media dir was emptied).
explain.jobs.ra_badges: Refreshes the RetroAchievements account's unlocks, then for each game fetches its achievements again where something was unlocked since, downloads every badge (colour and locked) into the cache and redraws the badge mosaic. Played: the account's games. Owned: games linked to a release you hold. Badge images come from RetroAchievements' image host and use no API allowance; refetching achievements does, one request per changed game.
tabinfo.config.ai: The AI that answers in the app (provider, model, API key), the Ask menu's first link, the prices for the approximate cost, and the saved answers.
